title: Callouts, clipboard images, and object ordering
summary: Add editable rectangular callouts, align text inside its box, copy the rendered image, and change which annotation appears in front.

Added: Rectangular callouts with editable text, RGBA fill and outline, padding, a movable pointer, and body resizing. Save and reopen them as editable projects.
Horizontal and vertical text alignment in the Text and Callout editing dialog, using the shared renderer and command history.
Copy All through the toolbar or Ctrl+Shift+C and New from Clipboard through Ctrl+Shift+N. Clipboard imports create a flattened, unsaved document.
Bring Forward, Bring to Front, Send Backward, and Send to Back in Image > Arrange. Ctrl+Shift+F/B move the selected annotation one position.
Improved: Arrange shortcuts respect text/property input, modal dialogs and active gestures. Boundary actions leave the document and history unchanged.
Full shortcut labels fit beside the temporary readiness badges. The responsive toolbar shows one Move control at compact and maximized sizes.
Successful file operations retain their folder for the current session; native dialog verification of this behavior remains pending.

limitations: This is an incremental alpha, not complete interface or behavioral parity. Red target labels remain on broader scopes that still need verification or more features.

Native editor, save/restart, rendering and clipboard pixel checks passed. Windows Save As/export dialog inspection is blocked by the inspection tool; folder retention and clipboard Save-and-continue were not fully exercised in this pass.
Callouts currently have one rectangular body and triangular pointer. Additional shapes, shadows, pointer styles and inline text entry remain planned; text still uses two bundled fonts and a dialog.

Object Cut/Copy/Paste, broader clipboard compatibility, align/flatten/flip/rotate, screen capture, global hotkeys, library and video remain unfinished. Folder preferences do not persist across restarts.

Windows x64 portable alpha; not code-signed. Editable projects retain original pixels; share flattened images when redacting content. Full reference layout, Windows snap layouts and maximized drag-to-restore remain incomplete.
